newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks close up as buyers shrug off rigging.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks close up as buyers shrug off rigging.

text.p: Dhaka stocks closed higher on Saturday as buyers shrugged off a recent scam in which big market players allegedly manipulated share prices but authorities later said the offenders will face penalty.

The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) all share price index closed 81.02 points or 6.99 percent up, the highest in recent weeks, at 1,238.6 on a turnover of 49.8 million taka. Of 119 traded issues 109 gained, six lost and four remained unchanged.
Bangladesh Lamps gained 401 taka to 4,416, Apex Foods rose 201 to 2,216 and Beximco Pharmaceuticals was up 15 to 165.

Newspapers said a report by a government-appointed committee on the alleged scam identified at least 20 dealers of the Dhaka and Chittagong stock exchanges who had manipulated share prices in October and November.
The DSE index at the time soared to more than 3,600 points.
Dr. Harunur Rashid, chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, said: "We will examine the inquiry committee report. I can assure you that law will take its own course."
A committee member told Reuters on Sunday top dealers and powerful brokers were involved in the scam.
SEC sources said the offenders could be fined and jailed, and might also lose their DSE or CSE (Chittagong Stock Exchange) membership.
Brokers who were not named in the report demanded punishment of the guilty.
Earlier it was feared that the market might suffer in the wake of the report.
"There is no reason for the market to fall further as prices of most scrips have reached their bottom levels. We have a lot of buying orders," said broker Shakil Rizvi.
